## Short Biography

**Jeppe Rich** is Professor at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU Management, Department of Technology, Management and Economics) specializing in large-scale transport modelling, optimization, and econometrics. Holding an M.Sc. in Mathematical Planning from the University of Aarhus (1995) and a Ph.D. from DTU (2001), he works across quantitative transportation science, including discrete choice and demand models, mixed-integer and stochastic optimization, population synthesis, charging infrastructure planning, freight electrification, and bicycle demand.

In March 2023, he was appointed Co-Editor-in-Chief and Founding Editor of the Elsevier journal *Journal of Cycling and Micromobility Research*, co-founded with Professor Eva Heinen. Throughout his career he has led numerous national and European transport modelling programmes, notably serving as chief designer for the **Danish National Transport Model (LTM)**, a €7 million venture. He is the recipient of the **2025 Danish Transport Research Prize**.

He collaborates closely with international academic partners (including TU Delft, NTNU, ETH Zurich, University of Leeds, KU, TUM, KTH, Tongji, Technion, and MIT) as well as ministries, public authorities, and the European Commission.

- **2020–2024:** Guest Professor, Southeast University, China.
- **2017–2021:** Member of the Committee for the Bibliometric Research Indicator (BFI).
- **2016–2019:** Advisory Board Member, *European Transport Research Review* (ETRR).

## Education & Academic Career at DTU

- **2016–present:** Professor, DTU Management, Department of Technology, Management and Economics (Section Leader, Demand Modelling Group 2018–2020; Professor with special responsibilities in large-scale transport models 2016).
- **2008–2016:** Associate Professor, DTU Transport (Coordinator of the Large-Scale Modelling team from 2014).
- **2002–2008:** Assistant Professor, Centre for Traffic and Transport, DTU (and Senior Consultant, Atkins Denmark A/S, 2002–2003).
- **2001:** Ph.D. in Transport Demand Modelling, Technical University of Denmark (*Long-term Travel Demand Modelling*).
- **1995–1998:** Researcher, National Environmental Research Institute (NERI), Ministry of the Environment.
- **1995:** M.Sc. in Mathematical Planning, University of Aarhus (*Spatial Econometric Models*).

## Public Outreach & Media Presence

Regular contributor to Danish public policy debates on infrastructure appraisal, road pricing, public transport fares, transport electrification, and cycling investments, with **50+ television, radio, and print interviews (2021–2025)** across *DR TV-Avisen*, *TV2 News*, *Altinget*, *Politiken*, *Berlingske*, *Ingeniøren*, and *Radio4*.
